strengths.s: You already know far more words than you are able to use under pressure. That is a good problem, because the words do not have to be learned again. They have to be made available faster.

You have opinions and you can find something to say on almost any topic. Many candidates lose marks because they have nothing to say. That is not your problem, which means the work is about delivery rather than about thinking.
You keep going rather than stopping when something is difficult. That single habit is worth more than it looks, because the marking rewards sustained speech.
You understand questions the first time and answer what was actually asked. Examiners notice this immediately, and it makes the whole conversation easier for both people.
Your speed is easy to follow, neither rushed nor slow. This is worth protecting when the other work starts.
You are interesting to listen to. The test is a conversation with a human being, and a human being who is enjoying the conversation is a friendlier marker.
You notice when something comes out wrong. That awareness is the foundation of every correction that follows, and many students do not have it.

weaknesses.meta: Big words slowing everything else down

units.name: Specificity, name it exactly
units.reason: the vocabulary is genuinely there. The issue is that it is being spent on rarity when the marking pays for precision. This exercise trains the difference.

units.name: Show, do not tell, the sensory sweep
units.reason: the nouns you choose are right almost every time. It is the words attached to them that are travelling in from your first language, and that is a partnering habit rather than a vocabulary gap.
